Feature discovery prompts have more impact when they reach the right people at a relevant moment. Shown to the wrong person at the wrong time, they feel intrusive.

The JavaScript component is Expressive.TapTarget. Put tap-target on the prompt and point data-target at the id of the element you want to highlight. AutoInit() starts every .tap-target except those marked no-autoinit. Clicking the origin toggles the prompt; Escape or a click outside the copy also closes it. You can also call open() and close().

The spotlight is 480px (360px on small screens). Override --md-comp-tap-target-size if you need it larger. Motion is CSS; prefers-reduced-motion drops the pulse and the scale.

Open tap target Close tap target

menu

I am here

Provide value and encourage return visits by introducing users to new features and functionality at contextually relevant moments.

<button type="button" id="menu" class="btn-floating btn-large">
  <i class="material-symbols">menu</i>
</button>
<div class="tap-target" data-target="menu">
  <h2>I am here</h2>
  <p>Introduce the control at a relevant moment.</p>
</div>

.tap-target-content is optional — init wraps loose children if it is missing. .feature-discovery is a style alias of .tap-target.

Initialization

The IIFE bundle exposes Expressive.TapTarget. Call init yourself when you need callbacks, or let Expressive.AutoInit() start every .tap-target. 

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  const elems = document.querySelectorAll('.tap-target');
  const instances = Expressive.TapTarget.init(elems, {
    // specify options here
  });
});

Per-instance options can also be passed through AutoInit:

Expressive.AutoInit(document.body, {
  TapTarget: {
    onOpen: function(origin) { /* ... */ }
  }
});

Options

Name Type Default Description
onOpen Function null Called when the tap target opens. Receives the origin element.
onClose Function null Called when the tap target closes. Receives the origin element.

Methods

All methods are called on the plugin instance. You can get the instance like this: 
const instance = Expressive.TapTarget.getInstance(elem);
.open();

Open the tap target.

instance.open();
.close();

Close the tap target.

instance.close();
.destroy();

Destroy the plugin instance and tear down its event handlers.

instance.destroy();

Properties

Name Type Description
el Element The DOM element the plugin was initialized with (the .tap-target).
originEl Element The highlighted origin, or null if data-target did not resolve.
options Object The options the instance was initialized with.
isOpen Boolean Whether the tap target is open.
